**Minimum 1 GB RAM; 2 GB recommended.** The server embeds its semantic engine in-process — `gte-multilingual-base` (Apache 2.0, ONNX q8, 768 dims), loaded at boot (~1.1 s from the baked image; a broken model fails the boot instead of degrading silently), ~730 MB total process RSS measured under embedding load, ~14 ms per embedding on CPU. That requirement buys the entire trade: **no external services, no API keys, no network calls** — semantic candidate detection (including cross-language matching) works out of the box on an air-gapped box. Disk: the image carries the model (+~300 MB). The full pipeline is diagrammed in docs/embeddings.md.
|`JUDGMENT_ORPHAN_AFTER_MS`|`86400000`|Age (ms) past which pending judgments with two `active` endpoints surface in `memory.context` for the agent to close. 24h.|
|`JUDGMENT_ORPHAN_DEADLINE_MS`|`1209600000`|Age (ms) past which unjudged pendings are orphaned by the sweep (journaled, undoable). 14 days.|
|`RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED`|`false`|Master toggle. `true` activates the limiter; misbehaving tokens get `429 rate_limited` with `Retry-After`.|
|`RATE_LIMIT_RPS`|`10`|Refill rate per token, in requests per second.|
|`RATE_LIMIT_BURST`|`30`|Burst capacity per token. The first N requests after a quiet period are free; beyond that, RPS applies.|
|`AUTH_LOCKOUT_MAX_FAILURES`|`10`|Failed auth attempts from one IP within the window before it is locked out (`429`).|
|`AUTH_LOCKOUT_MS`|`60000`|Lockout duration (ms) once tripped. A successful auth clears the identity's counter.|
|`MAX_BODY_BYTES`|`4194304`|Max raw request body on `/mcp` and `/api`; larger is rejected with `413`.|
|`REMBRIC_MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS`|_unset_|Comma-separated `Host` allow-list (incl. port) for opt-in DNS-rebinding protection on the MCP transport. When set, requests with an unlisted `Host` are rejected.|

Day-to-day operator work lives in the dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:8787/dashboard (port `8788` in the dev stack). Mint and revoke API tokens at `/dashboard/tokens`, create and archive projects at `/dashboard/projects`, soft-delete agent sessions at `/dashboard/sessions`, browse and soft-delete curated user prompts at `/dashboard/prompts` (FTS5 search over content + tags; refined predecessors show a `REFINED` badge), trigger consolidation at `/dashboard/consolidation`, and run the operator-only purges from `/dashboard/maintenance`. Programmatic agents talk to the same data through the MCP `project.*` / `memory.*` tools or, for admin-only operations, through the HTTP endpoints under `/admin/*` (admin bearer token required — see docs/agents.md).

- **Project scoping by construction**: every memory is attached to exactly one `project_id`. Consolidation, relations and every write never cross scope. One read may, and only when asked: `memory.search({across_projects: true})` reads the projects the connection's token is authorized to read and names them in `searchedProjects[]` — opt-in, read-only, and a compile error on any write path. See docs/agents.md.

Memory also exposes a **derived review state** alongside decay: a `needs_review` flag on `memory.search` / `memory.get_batch` rows (and a `needsReview[]` list in `memory.context`) for active memories whose per-type shelf life elapsed without re-affirmation. It is computed at read time — no column, no sweep — and is cleared by re-affirming with `memory.confirm_batch` (not by merely reading). See docs/relations.md for the relation taxonomy and the review axis.

|Customer workspace|Protected `/app` area, `/app/license` and `/app/settings`. Accounts without a licence see the landing page's tier cards with regional prices and the course lessons a purchase unlocks (counted from D1), and start checkout in one press, with their email already filled in; a tier picked on the landing page carries through sign-up. After payment the workspace waits for the licence to activate. Licence owners see their key with the CLI commands that activate, show and free a machine, their machine activations, and activation deactivation. In `/app/settings` a customer picks the time zone that every date in the workspace is shown in.|

|Billing|Authenticated Polar checkout for the Core, Complete, and Agency tiers with regional (PPP) discounts, returning the buyer to the workspace in their language, and webhook handling for purchases, full refunds (a partial refund keeps the licence), and licence-key benefits; a full refund marks the licence refunded and a revoked benefit marks it revoked. One licence per account: checkout is refused while a licence is active, and Polar's checkout endpoint is reachable only through that server-side check. Requires configured provider products and credentials.|

|CLI licence API|The API that the `saasyland` CLI calls under `/api/cli/v1` to read a licence, to activate, check and release machines and to download the template bundle of a release. It is built on the `@saasyland/stack/api` contract, which the CLI imports too: the key is checked against D1, machines are Polar activations identified by an HMAC of the machine ID, activating again from the same machine reuses its slot, bundles come from a private R2 bucket through short-lived signed URLs, and requests are rate-limited per IP address and per licence key. See the CLI licence API guide.|

|Newsletter|Double opt-in subscription with localized email delivery, limited per recipient. The confirmation and unsubscribe links open a page that acts only when the visitor presses its button. Server functions read and change a signed-in user's subscription, but no workspace screen uses them yet.|

|Admin users and security|Database-backed user listing, password reset, ban/unban, and deletion. The settings security tab connects password changes, TOTP, and session revocation, and the general tab saves the admin's own time zone.|
|Products and categories|D1 schemas, permission-checked CRUD use cases, and database-backed lists. Product creation/publishing controls are not fully connected.|

|Courses|A public catalogue at `/courses` with course and lesson pages backed by D1 (`course`, `chapter`, `lesson`, and `lesson_progress`). Each lesson is a free preview, free with an account, or paid (an active Complete or Agency licence); the server functions enforce access, and admins can watch every lesson. The player resumes where the viewer stopped and saves progress. Admins create and edit courses, chapters, and lessons at `/admin/courses`, where each lesson picks its video from the library. The landing page lists the published courses and their first lessons from D1, links each to its page, and plays a tour of the course pages. See the Courses guide.|

|Videos|Recordings are encoded on your machine to adaptive HLS with FFmpeg (`bun run video:publish:<environment>`), stored in a private R2 bucket, and streamed through signed, expiring `/media/` links with the Workers cache and range requests. `/admin/videos` lists, previews, and deletes them, and course lessons play them. |Affiliates|Referral links tracked by Affonso, loaded only on visits that carry a referral parameter; checkout passes the referral to Polar as order metadata, so commissions follow Polar's own order and refund records. `/affiliates` publishes the terms.
